manifest.name: dsh-labview
manifest.description: Open password-protected LabVIEW VI/CTL block diagrams without LabVIEW or Python. A byte-exact engine that clears the BDPW password block and the library-protected flag, with backups and verification.
manifest.author: yxfvvv

bundle.text:
# The dsh-labview bundle patch. Applied after @deepseek-ai/dsh-base and
# before the profile's own cordis.patch.yml, so this row can be overridden by id
# in a later layer.
#
# One host-plane row: the service plus the three model tools (lv_scan,
# lv_unlock, lv_restore). Tools register on the host `tools` registry, so every
# agent sees them; each call resolves the target directory from the session
# workspace or an explicit argument.
#
# Keep this file a PLAIN `id`/`name` insert. The plugin market hot-mounts a
# bundle row so its on/off switch applies without a restart, and that path
# accepts only bare `id`/`name` rows — a `config:` block, an `inject:` line, a
# disable, or an expression makes the whole patch read as "contains config /
# expression rows" and every toggle falls back to restart activation.
#
# Nothing is lost by keeping it bare: every option is already the schema default
# in lib/index.js, and the module declares `inject = ['tools']`. To override an
# option, set it in your profile's cordis.patch.yml (row id `labview-unlock`).
- insert:
    - id: labview-unlock
      name: dsh-labview

readme.text:
**Open password-protected LabVIEW block diagrams — without LabVIEW, without Python.**

Inherited a LabVIEW project whose front panels open but whose block diagrams are
locked? This plugin removes that protection from `*.vi`, `*.ctl`, `*.vit` and
`*.ctt` files by patching a few bytes in place. No gigabytes of NI runtime, no
`pylabview`, no network — just a small, dependency-free JavaScript engine.

```
lv_scan      what is locked, and which LabVIEW version saved each file
lv_unlock    back up, patch, verify, write
lv_restore   put the originals back
```

---

LabVIEW "password protection" is not encryption. The diagram is stored in the
file in the clear; what stops you from opening it is a small bookkeeping block:

| Block | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BDPW` | `md5(password)` + `hash_1` + `hash_2` — the password record |
| `LVSR` | version block; `execFlags` bit 13 (`LibProtected`, `0x2000`) marks a locked library |

Give LabVIEW an empty password and matching hashes and it opens the diagram
without asking. That is exactly what this plugin writes:

1. `password_md5` → `md5("")` = `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`
2. `hash_1` → `md5(md5("") ‖ LIBN ‖ LVSR ‖ salt)`
3. `hash_2` → `md5(hash_1 ‖ contentHash(BDH))`
4. clear `VI_EXEC_FLAGS.LibProtected` in `LVSR`

The only unknown is the 12-byte `salt`, which LabVIEW derives from the counts of
terminal types in the connector pane. Rather than parse the type descriptors, the
engine brute-forces the three small integers against the hashes already stored in
the file — a typical count is under 20, so most files resolve in a few
milliseconds.

Nothing else in the file is touched: no re-serialization, no re-compression, no
length changes. A file that was not locked is left byte-identical.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-labview     # from npm, after it is published
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-labview   # local checkout
```

Restart the harness (or toggle the plugin in the market page) and the three tools
appear in every session.

Ask in plain language — "unlock the LabVIEW files in this project" — or call the
tools directly.

```
lv_scan(dir?, lockedOnly?)
```

Read-only survey. Reports, per file, the LabVIEW version, whether the block
diagram is protected, whether it can be unlocked, and why not when it cannot.
Uses no writes, so it is safe on a production copy.

```
lv_unlock(dir?, dryRun?, hashSource?, limit?)
```

Backs up every original into `<dir>/_lv_unlock_backup/…`, patches the file, and
**verifies the patched bytes in memory before touching the disk**. Already-open
files are counted and skipped. `dryRun: true` reports what would happen and
writes nothing — always worth doing first on a large tree.

```
lv_restore(dir?, dryRun?, limit?)
```

Copies the backups back over the working files, undoing an unlock.

> Scan `D:\SCADA\FC MAS V1` for locked LabVIEW files, then unlock them and tell
> me which LabVIEW version I need to open the project.

The model runs `lv_scan`, sees `140 × LabVIEW 2015 / 83 × LabVIEW 8.5`, runs
`lv_unlock`, and reports both. Originals stay in `_lv_unlock_backup/` until you
delete them.

- **Backup first.** The original is copied to the backup tree before the first
  byte is written. An existing backup is never overwritten, so a second
  `lv_unlock` cannot destroy the pristine copy.
- **Verify, then write.** The patched buffer is re-parsed and must report
  "no password" before it reaches the file. Anything unexpected is refused.
- **Atomic writes.** Bytes land through `<file>.lvunlock.tmp` + rename, so an
  interrupted run cannot leave a half-written VI.
- **Only two edits.** `lv_unlock` reports the exact byte ranges it changed for
  every file; a file that needs no change is never rewritten.
- **No LabVIEW required.** The engine parses the RSRC container directly. It
  never runs the VI, never decompiles the diagram, and never needs a license.

Files saved by **LabVIEW 8.0 through 2019** (and older files that were last saved
by those releases). LabVIEW 2020+ changed the block layout; those files are
reported as unsupported instead of being written.

Version handling has one subtlety worth knowing: removing a password also clears
`LibProtected`, and LabVIEW hashes the version block *after* that change — so
`hash_1` covers the cleared flags. VIs last saved by old releases keep a legacy
version-block layout where the flag never made it into the hash. The engine
detects this (`hashSource: "auto"`) and reproduces the matching behaviour;
`"final"` or `"original"` force one or the other.

The engine is not a guess: it was validated byte-for-byte against a reference
implementation on real industrial code.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Files re-unlocked from pristine originals and compared byte-for-byte | **223 / 223 identical** |
| Random spot audits of a previous 601-file project | 597 unlocked, 0 remaining locked |
| Password-salt recovery proved correct (re-derives the hashes already in every file) | 223 / 223 |
| Files modified by mistake | 0 — every diff was the password block plus one flag byte |

Average 35 ms per file; the slowest file (a large VI with an unlucky salt) takes
about 0.9 s.

Every option has a working default; override only if you want to.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `backupDir` | `_lv_unlock_backup` | Backup directory, relative to the scanned root |
| `extensions` | `.vi .ctl .vit .ctt .xctl` | File types to process |
| `maxFiles` | `20000` | Safety cap on a single scan |
| `concurrency` | `4` | Files processed in parallel |
| `hashSource` | `auto` | Which version block the new hash covers (`auto`/`final`/`original`) |

```yaml

- id: labview-unlock
  config:
    backupDir: _lv_backup
    concurrency: 8
```

- **No in-app verification.** The plugin cannot open LabVIEW, so "unlocked" means
  the file's own password record says so. Open one file in LabVIEW before
  trusting a bulk run on an irreplaceable project.
- **Salt brute force has a ceiling.** Counts are searched up to 255 each
  (≈16.7 M combinations). Pathological connector panes beyond that are reported
  as not unlockable rather than silently mishandled.
- **Type definitions.** Unlocking a `*.ctl` exposes its diagram too — as with
  any password removal, types the project used as opaque boxes can now be edited.
- **Ethics.** Use this only on software you own or are authorized to maintain.
  Recovering access to a project your company paid for is maintenance; defeating
  a vendor's licensing is not.

The harness ships an Electron binary that runs as Node, which is handy on
machines without a separate Node install:

```bash
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "…/DSH Desktop.exe" test/verify-223.mjs <project dir>
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "…/DSH Desktop.exe" test/smoke.mjs <dir with locked VIs>
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "…/DSH Desktop.exe" test/harness-swap.mjs
```

`assets/make-icon.mjs` renders the icon with no image dependency.

Publishing steps (npm, GitHub, marketplace PR) are in [PUBLISHING.md](PUBLISHING.md).

`lib/engine.js` is standalone — import it from `dsh-labview/engine` to use
the parser and patcher without the harness.
